Equality holds if and only if the ambient distribution has zero variance in the normal directions (<math id="Thmtheorem1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{N}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{N}=0</annotation></semantics></math>).</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W\sim\mathcal{N}(\hat{U},\Sigma_{A})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W\sim\mathcal{N}(\hat{U},\Sigma_{A})</annotation></semantics></math>. We orthogonally decompose <math id="S4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}+\xi_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}+\xi_{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{T}\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{T}\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{N}\in N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{N}\in N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math>. By definition of the normal space, <math id="S4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{N}=\hat{U}S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{N}=\hat{U}S</annotation></semantics></math> for some symmetric matrix <math id="S4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">As rigorously derived in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Proof Details for Theorem ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>, the polar projection <math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\pi(W)=W(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(W)=W(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> maps the ambient perturbation to the manifold. Taylor expanding to second order, the projected sample is:</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{proj}}=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}-\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}\xi_{T}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})+O(\|\xi\|^{3})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{proj}}=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}-\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}\xi_{T}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})+O(\|\xi\|^{3})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the first three terms precisely match the intrinsic retraction <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi(\xi_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi(\xi_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>, and the structural discrepancy is <math id="S4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S+\frac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S+\frac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>. Crucially, <math id="S4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> lies entirely within the tangent space.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Because <math id="S4.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{T}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{T}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma_{T})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> are independent zero-mean variables, <math id="S4.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is a zero-mean heteroskedastic noise term conditionally dependent on <math id="S4.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, <math id="S4.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{proj}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{proj}}</annotation></semantics></math> represents a conditionally mean-preserving stochastic spread of the optimal tangent sample <math id="S4.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\mathrm{tang}}=\phi(\xi_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ϕ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\mathrm{tang}}=\phi(\xi_{T})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">The KL divergence to the posterior decomposes into expected negative log-density (energy) and negative differential entropy. Because <math id="S4.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\mathrm{post}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>post</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\mathrm{post}}</annotation></semantics></math> is highly concentrated, its local energy is characterized closely by <math id="S4.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}\|\tilde{\xi}_{T}\|_{H}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ξ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\|\tilde{\xi}_{T}\|_{H}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S4.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H=\Sigma_{T}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>T</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H=\Sigma_{T}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>. The expected energy of <math id="S4.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\mathrm{proj}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\mathrm{proj}}</annotation></semantics></math> inflates additively:</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{q_{\mathrm{proj}}}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\tilde{\xi}_{T}\|_{H}^{2}]\approx\mathbb{E}_{q_{\mathrm{tang}}}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\xi_{T}\|_{H}^{2}]+\mathbb{E}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\Delta\|_{H}^{2}]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>ξ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝔼</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{q_{\mathrm{proj}}}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\tilde{\xi}_{T}\|_{H}^{2}]\approx\mathbb{E}_{q_{\mathrm{tang}}}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\xi_{T}\|_{H}^{2}]+\mathbb{E}[\tfrac{1}{2}\|\Delta\|_{H}^{2}].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">Concurrently, injecting conditional mean-zero noise <math id="S4.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mid\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo fence="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mid\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> into a Gaussian distribution inherently increases its differential entropy. However, by standard information-theoretic expansions of entropy under multiplicative noise mixtures, the entropy gain is bounded tightly by the linear trace term <math id="S4.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}[\|\Delta\|_{H}^{2}]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>𝔼</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{E}[\|\Delta\|_{H}^{2}]</annotation></semantics></math>, leaving a strictly positive quadratic residual.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Consequently, the linear energy penalty strictly outpaces the entropy increase, guaranteeing that the KL divergence grows:</span></p>
<table id="S4.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{post}})\approx\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{post}})+\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{tr}\big((H\,\mathrm{Cov}(\Delta\mid\xi_{T}))^{2}\big)\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>post</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>≈</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>post</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>tr</mi><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>H</mi><mi>Cov</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{post}})\approx\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{post}})+\frac{1}{4}\mathbb{E}\!\left[\mathrm{tr}\big((H\,\mathrm{Cov}(\Delta\mid\xi_{T}))^{2}\big)\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">This excess penalty <math id="S4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly positive whenever both <math id="S4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> are non-zero, demonstrating that normal-space variance systematically degrades the manifold posterior approximation.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The practical implication is clear: any posterior variance that leaks into the normal space of <math id="S4.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>St</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> is wasted at best and mathematically harmful at worst, since it introduces systematic variance distortion in the projected samples. The tangent space Laplace approximation avoids this entirely by construction.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p8.1" class="ltx_p">To quantify the gap empirically, we compute both <math id="S4.p8.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ML</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S4.p8.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ML</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})</annotation></semantics></math> via Monte Carlo estimation (<math id="S4.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> samples) on the MNLI adapter weights after training on LLaMA-2-7B.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span>Empirical KL gap between tangent space and projected approximations across representative adapter layers (MNLI, LLaMA-2-7B). <math id="S4.T1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\Delta\mathrm{KL}=\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})-\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>KL</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ML</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>ML</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathrm{KL}=\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})-\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}}\|p_{\mathrm{ML}})</annotation></semantics></math> in nats. Posterior spread is the trace of the tangent space covariance.</figcaption>
<table id="S4.T1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S4.T1.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T1.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt">Layer</th>
<th id="S4.T1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><math id="S4.T1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>tang</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{tang}})</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<th id="S4.T1.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><math id="S4.T1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>proj</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(q_{\mathrm{proj}})</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<th id="S4.T1.2.1.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt"><math id="S4.T1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta\mathrm{KL}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>KL</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta\mathrm{KL}</annotation></semantics></math></th></tr>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> confirms that the theoretical advantage translates to a measurable practical difference. The gap is largest in early layers (4.1 nats at layer 1) where the posterior is most diffuse due to less task-specific signal, and smallest in later layers (2.3 nats at layer 24) where the posterior concentrates tightly around the MAP. This pattern is consistent with Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Geometric Variance Inflation &amp; KL Tightness). ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>: the excess KL penalty <math id="S4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{E}(\Sigma_{T},\Sigma_{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{E}(\Sigma_{T},\Sigma_{N})</annotation></semantics></math> grows with the posterior spread, since wider posteriors have more variance available to leak into the normal space.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 1</span></span><span id="Thmremark1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Choice of retraction)<span id="Thmremark1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmremark1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Geometric Variance Inflation &amp; KL Tightness). ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> holds for any retraction that agrees with the exponential map to second order. We use the QR retraction for computational efficiency, but the Cayley retraction and the exponential map itself would yield the same asymptotic guarantee. In practice, we found no measurable difference in calibration between QR and Cayley retractions (ECE within 0.001 on MNLI), so we use QR throughout for its simplicity.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Experiments</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate SBA across three dimensions of reliability—calibration, selective prediction, and out-of-distribution detection—on two model families to confirm that the benefits of geometric priors are not architecture-specific, and we include a generative task to demonstrate applicability beyond classification.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Setup</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use five base models spanning four architecture families: RoBERTa-large <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2019</a>)</cite> (355M parameters, encoder-only), LLaMA-2-7B and LLaMA-2-13B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023</a>)</cite> (decoder-only), Mistral-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">Jiang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> (decoder-only with grouped-query attention and sliding window attention), and Qwen2.5-7B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qwen Team, 2024</a>)</cite> (decoder-only with a different tokenizer, training corpus, and architecture from both LLaMA and Mistral). RoBERTa and LLaMA-2-7B are evaluated on the full benchmark suite; Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-7B, and LLaMA-2-13B are evaluated on MNLI and SST-2 to validate cross-family and cross-scale generalization. Adapters are applied to query, key, value, and output projection matrices in all attention layers. The adapter rank is <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=16</annotation></semantics></math> unless otherwise noted. All results report mean <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation across 5 random seeds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We compare against nine baselines spanning deterministic, Bayesian, ensemble, and post-hoc approaches: LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite>, DoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, OrthoLoRA (Stiefel-constrained factors, deterministic), Laplace-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Daxberger et al., 2024</a>)</cite> (flat-space Laplace over LoRA weights), MC-Drop-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">Gal and Ghahramani, 2016</a>)</cite> (MC-Dropout with <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>), SWAG-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">Maddox et al., 2019</a>)</cite> (Stochastic Weight Averaging Gaussian), Gauss+Proj (Gaussian prior in <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{d\times k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{d\times k}</annotation></semantics></math> with polar projection to <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>St</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math>), Deep-Ens-LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lakshminarayanan et al., 2017</a>)</cite> (ensemble of 5 independently trained LoRA models), and temperature scaling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2017</a>)</cite> applied to LoRA as a post-hoc calibration baseline.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We assess task performance (accuracy, F1) on GLUE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2019b</a>)</cite> and SuperGLUE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2019a</a>)</cite> benchmarks, calibration (ECE <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">Naeini et al., 2015</a>)</cite> with 15 bins, Brier score, NLL), selective prediction (AUROC of the uncertainty-vs-correctness curve <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Akter et al., 2025</a>)</cite>), and OOD detection (AUROC using predictive entropy as the scoring function).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">All methods are trained for 3 epochs with AdamW (lr <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=2\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=2\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>), batch size 16, on 4<math id="S5.SS1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math>A100 GPUs. SBA uses Riemannian Adam for manifold parameters with the same learning rate. Prior concentration is set to <math id="S5.SS1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> (ablated in Section <a href="#S5.SS6" title="5.6 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.6</span></a>). For the Riemannian optimizer, we project the Euclidean gradient onto the tangent space at each step and apply the QR retraction, following the standard Riemannian SGD framework of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Absil et al. (2008)</a></cite>. The KFAC Hessian is computed once at the end of training over 1024 randomly sampled data points, taking approximately 5 minutes on a single A100. Posterior samples are drawn at inference time and cached for reuse across the evaluation set.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>In-Distribution Results</h3>

Best result in each column is bolded, second best underlined. <math id="S5.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math> indicates lower is better.</figcaption>

</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.2 In-Distribution Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows that SBA achieves task performance within 0.1–0.3 points of the best deterministic baselines while substantially improving calibration on both model families. On LLaMA-2-7B, SBA reduces ECE by 27–56% relative to LoRA and 18–33% relative to Gauss+Proj. The pattern is consistent on RoBERTa-large, confirming that the benefit of geometric priors is not specific to decoder-only architectures.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The comparison against Deep-Ens-LoRA deserves particular attention. The ensemble uses <math id="S5.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math> the adapter parameters and requires five independent training runs, yet SBA matches or slightly outperforms it on calibration while using a single set of adapter weights. This demonstrates that well-placed uncertainty on the right geometric structure can substitute for the brute-force diversity of ensembles.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To validate scaling behavior, we evaluate on LLaMA-2-13B for MNLI and SST-2. On MNLI, SBA achieves accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.1_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>90.1</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.1_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".024_{\pm.002}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.024</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.002</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.024_{\pm.002}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.3_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>90.3</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.3_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".057_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.057</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.057_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and Gauss+Proj at <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.8_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>89.8</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.8_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".033_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.033</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.033_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. On SST-2, SBA achieves accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.1_{\pm.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>96.1</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.1_{\pm.1}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".012_{\pm.001}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.012</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.001</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.012_{\pm.001}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="96.2_{\pm.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>96.2</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">96.2_{\pm.1}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".028_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.028</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.028_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. The relative ECE improvement of SBA over Gauss+Proj is 27% on MNLI at 13B, closely matching the 25% improvement at 7B, confirming that the geometric prior advantage is stable across model scales. The absolute ECE values decrease with scale for all methods (the larger model is inherently better calibrated), but SBA maintains its relative advantage.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To validate cross-family generalization, we evaluate on Mistral-7B, which uses grouped-query attention and sliding window attention rather than LLaMA’s standard multi-head attention. On MNLI, SBA achieves accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.8_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>89.8</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.8_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".025_{\pm.002}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.025</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.002</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.025_{\pm.002}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.9_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>89.9</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.9_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".055_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.055</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.055_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and Gauss+Proj at <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.5_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>89.5</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.5_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".034_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.034</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.034_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. On SST-2, SBA achieves accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.6_{\pm.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>95.6</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.6_{\pm.1}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".013_{\pm.001}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.013</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.001</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.013_{\pm.001}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.7_{\pm.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>95.7</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.7_{\pm.1}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".030_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.030</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.030_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. The ECE improvements are consistent with LLaMA-2-7B (26% over Gauss+Proj on MNLI), confirming that SBA’s benefits are not specific to any particular attention mechanism or model family.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">On Qwen2.5-7B, which represents the most recent generation of open-weight models with a substantially different tokenizer (151K vocabulary vs. 32K for LLaMA) and training corpus, SBA achieves accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.2_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>90.2</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.2_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".023_{\pm.002}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.023</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.002</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.023_{\pm.002}</annotation></semantics></math> on MNLI and accuracy <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95.8_{\pm.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>95.8</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95.8_{\pm.1}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".012_{\pm.001}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.012</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.001</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.012_{\pm.001}</annotation></semantics></math> on SST-2, compared to LoRA at <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="90.3_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>90.3</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">90.3_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".052_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.052</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.052_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and Gauss+Proj at <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="89.9_{\pm.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>89.9</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">89.9_{\pm.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="S5.SS2.p5.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".031_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.031</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.031_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. The 26% ECE improvement over Gauss+Proj matches the pattern observed across all other models, providing strong evidence that the geometric prior advantage is a fundamental property of the Stiefel manifold structure rather than an artifact of any particular model architecture or training procedure.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17809v1/fig2_reliability_diagrams.svg" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/196;" width="476" height="196"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span>Reliability diagrams on MNLI (in-distribution, top) and MNLI <math id="S5.F2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI (domain shift, bottom). SBA maintains calibration under shift while other methods degrade.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.2 In-Distribution Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> shows reliability diagrams for the key methods. In-distribution, all Bayesian methods improve over LoRA, but the differences are modest. Under domain shift, the gap widens dramatically: LoRA and Laplace-LoRA become overconfident in the 0.7–0.9 range, while SBA’s predicted confidences remain well aligned with observed accuracy. Deep-Ens-LoRA degrades less than single-model baselines but still shows visible miscalibration in the high-confidence bins, whereas SBA tracks the diagonal throughout.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Domain Shift Results</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The most important evaluation for reliability is behavior under distribution shift, where models encounter data that differs systematically from the training distribution. We evaluate on three shift scenarios: MNLI <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI (natural language inference across dataset boundaries), Amazon <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> Yelp (sentiment classification across review domains), and SQuAD <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> AdversarialQA (question answering under adversarial perturbation, evaluated with EM and F1 in addition to calibration).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Domain shift results on LLaMA-2-7B: calibration (ECE<math id="S5.T3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\downarrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↓</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\downarrow</annotation></semantics></math>) and selective prediction (Sel. AUROC<math id="S5.T3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\uparrow" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">↑</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\uparrow</annotation></semantics></math>). <th id="S5.T3.2.1.7.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row">Temp. Scal.</th>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.7.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.T3.m40" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".064_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.064</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.064_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.7.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">—</td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.7.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.T3.m41" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".079_{\pm.005}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.079</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.005</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.079_{\pm.005}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.7.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">—</td>

<td id="S5.T3.2.1.7.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center">—</td></tr>
<tr id="S5.T3.2.1.8" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T3.2.1.8.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t">SBA (Ours)</th>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m43" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.049_{\pm.003}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.049</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.049_{\pm.003}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m44" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.821_{\pm.007}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.821</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.007</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.821_{\pm.007}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.4" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m45" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.058_{\pm.003}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.058</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.058_{\pm.003}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.5" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m46" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.798_{\pm.008}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.798</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.008</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.798_{\pm.008}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.6" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m47" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.075_{\pm.004}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.075</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.075_{\pm.004}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="S5.T3.2.1.8.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb ltx_border_t"><math id="S5.T3.m48" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{.782_{\pm.009}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.782</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn class="ltx_mathvariant_bold" mathvariant="bold">.009</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{.782_{\pm.009}}</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Under domain shift, SBA’s advantage grows substantially (Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.3 Domain Shift Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). Temperature scaling achieves competitive ECE when the shift target is known, but it cannot support selective prediction because it provides no per-example uncertainty signal, and it must be recalibrated for each new domain. Deep-Ens-LoRA is the strongest baseline, yet SBA outperforms it by 2–3 points on selective AUROC while using <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math> fewer adapter parameters. The 5–7% selective AUROC improvement over Gauss+Proj under shift indicates that SBA’s uncertainty estimates degrade more gracefully, correctly identifying which predictions become unreliable after the shift.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For the SQuAD <math id="S5.SS3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> AdversarialQA shift, SBA achieves EM/F1 of 41.2/52.8 compared to 40.8/52.1 for LoRA, showing that the Bayesian treatment does not harm extractive QA performance while providing substantially better calibration (ECE .075 vs. .142).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17809v1/fig3_selective_prediction.svg" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/328;" width="476" height="328"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span>Selective prediction on MNLI <math id="S5.F3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI. SBA’s uncertainty estimates enable more effective abstention at all coverage levels.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 5.3 Domain Shift Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows the accuracy-at-coverage curves for the MNLI <math id="S5.SS3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI shift. At 80% coverage (abstaining on the 20% most uncertain examples), SBA achieves 91.2% accuracy compared to 87.8% for LoRA and 89.5% for Deep-Ens-LoRA. At 50% coverage, SBA reaches 95.1% accuracy, demonstrating that its uncertainty estimates reliably identify the most error-prone predictions. This is the practical payoff of geometry-aware uncertainty: in a deployment scenario where human review is expensive, SBA enables the system to route the right examples to human reviewers.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SBA achieves the strongest OOD detection across both far-OOD and near-OOD settings (Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.4 OOD Detection ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>). The near-OOD setting (SST-2 vs. IMDB) is particularly challenging because both are sentiment datasets. SBA’s 2.3-point improvement over Deep-Ens-LoRA and 4.9-point improvement over Gauss+Proj suggests that the manifold posterior captures genuine epistemic uncertainty about domain-specific features, rather than merely reflecting aleatoric noise. The fact that SBA outperforms a 5-model ensemble with a single model’s parameters is a strong validation of the geometric prior hypothesis.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Generative Task: Abstractive Summarization</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To demonstrate that SBA’s benefits extend beyond classification, we evaluate on XSum abstractive summarization using LLaMA-2-7B. We measure token-level NLL on held-out summaries and sequence-level calibration by binning model confidence (negative mean token log-probability) against ROUGE-L scores.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">SBA achieves ROUGE-L of <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38.2_{\pm 0.4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>38.2</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38.2_{\pm 0.4}</annotation></semantics></math> (vs. <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="38.4_{\pm 0.3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>38.4</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">38.4_{\pm 0.3}</annotation></semantics></math> for LoRA, within noise), while reducing token-level NLL from <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.41_{\pm.03}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>2.41</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.03</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.41_{\pm.03}</annotation></semantics></math> (LoRA) to <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.33_{\pm.02}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>2.33</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.02</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.33_{\pm.02}</annotation></semantics></math> and sequence-level ECE from <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".089_{\pm.006}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.089</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.006</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.089_{\pm.006}</annotation></semantics></math> (LoRA) to <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".061_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.061</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.061_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math>. Laplace-LoRA achieves NLL <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.37_{\pm.03}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>2.37</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.03</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.37_{\pm.03}</annotation></semantics></math> and ECE <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".074_{\pm.005}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.074</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.005</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.074_{\pm.005}</annotation></semantics></math>, and Gauss+Proj achieves NLL <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.35_{\pm.03}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>2.35</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.03</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.35_{\pm.03}</annotation></semantics></math> and ECE <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".069_{\pm.005}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.069</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.005</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.069_{\pm.005}</annotation></semantics></math>. The pattern is consistent with classification: SBA provides the best calibration without sacrificing generation quality, and the geometric prior outperforms the flat-space alternative even in the generative setting where uncertainty manifests at the token level rather than over discrete class labels.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We also examine the uncertainty decomposition on XSum. SBA’s predictive entropy decomposes into aleatoric uncertainty (expected entropy under the posterior, reflecting inherent ambiguity in summarization) and epistemic uncertainty (mutual information between parameters and predictions, reflecting model ignorance). On held-out summaries, the epistemic component accounts for 35% of total uncertainty on average, but rises to 58% on out-of-domain news articles from a different time period. This confirms that SBA’s manifold posterior captures genuine epistemic uncertainty that is informative about distribution shift, even in the generative setting (Figure <a href="#S5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 5.5 Generative Task: Abstractive Summarization ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2602.17809v1/fig4_uncertainty_decomposition.svg" id="S5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/181;" width="476" height="181"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span>Uncertainty decomposition across settings. Epistemic uncertainty (mutual information) rises sharply under domain shift and on OOD data, while aleatoric uncertainty remains stable. SBA captures genuine model ignorance that flat-space methods underestimate.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6 </span>Ablation Studies</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct ablations on MNLI with LLaMA-2-7B to understand which components of SBA contribute most. All ablations report mean <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> std over 5 seeds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Varying prior concentration <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}\in\{0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0,5.0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}\in\{0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0,5.0\}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECE improves monotonically from <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>, then plateaus. Task accuracy remains stable (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 0.2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 0.2</annotation></semantics></math>) across the range.</p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The value <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}=1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}=1.0</annotation></semantics></math> offers the best tradeoff and is used in all other experiments (Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.6 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). The robustness across <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}\in[0.5,5.0]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}\in[0.5,5.0]</annotation></semantics></math> is reassuring: the method is not sensitive to this hyperparameter.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Selective prediction AUROC saturates at <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=5</annotation></semantics></math> posterior samples (within 0.3% of <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=50</annotation></semantics></math>), making SBA practical for deployment. ECE continues to improve slightly up to <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=20</annotation></semantics></math>, but the marginal gain from <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=20</annotation></semantics></math> is only 0.001, so we use <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> as the default.</p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 5.6 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> shows the full sample count ablation. The diminishing returns beyond <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> are clear: the ECE improvement from <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=50" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>50</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=50</annotation></semantics></math> is only 0.001, while the cost increases <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math>. For applications where only selective prediction is needed (not full calibration), <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=5</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficient and reduces the inference overhead to a level comparable with a 5-model ensemble.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p6.1" class="ltx_p">At adapter rank <math id="S5.SS6.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=4</annotation></semantics></math>, SBA still outperforms Laplace-LoRA at <math id="S5.SS6.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=16</annotation></semantics></math> on calibration metrics (ECE .033 vs. .039), suggesting that the geometric prior provides strong regularization even at very low rank (Table <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.6 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>).</p>
</div>

</figure>
<div id="S5.SS6.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p8.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T8" title="Table 8 ‣ 5.6 Ablation Studies ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> reveals that the orthonormal factors <math id="S5.SS6.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS6.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>V</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V</annotation></semantics></math> carry the vast majority of the calibration benefit, while the singular values <math id="S5.SS6.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> contribute only marginally. Making only <math id="S5.SS6.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>U</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U</annotation></semantics></math> Bayesian captures 85% of the calibration gain at 60% of the inference cost, offering a favorable tradeoff for compute-constrained settings. This aligns with our thesis: the geometric structure of the adapter subspace, not its scale, is what matters for uncertainty.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p9.1" class="ltx_p">We also ablate the choice of Hessian approximation. Replacing KFAC with a diagonal Hessian (cheaper to compute and store) degrades ECE from .027 to .031, a modest loss that may be acceptable when memory is constrained. Using the full (non-factored) Hessian is intractable for <math id="S5.SS6.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d&gt;256" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>256</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d&gt;256</annotation></semantics></math> but on a small-scale experiment (<math id="S5.SS6.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=128</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS6.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=8</annotation></semantics></math>) yields ECE .026, confirming that KFAC captures most of the curvature information.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we examine the sensitivity to the number of Hessian data points. Using 256 points (instead of 1024) degrades ECE from .027 to .029, while using 4096 points yields .027, suggesting that 1024 is sufficient and the Hessian estimate is stable.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.7 </span>Predictive Distillation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To address the <math id="S5.SS7.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="S\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\times</annotation></semantics></math> inference cost, we train a deterministic OrthoLoRA model to match SBA’s averaged predictive distribution via KL-divergence minimization on the training set.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T9" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 9: </span>Predictive distillation results (MNLI, LLaMA-2-7B).
