<div id="S5.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The distilled model retains 80% of the calibration improvement at <math id="S5.SS7.p2.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="1\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\times</annotation></semantics></math> inference cost (Table <a href="#S5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 5.7 Predictive Distillation ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>). Under domain shift (MNLI <math id="S5.SS7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI), the distilled model achieves ECE .059 (vs. .049 for SBA and .087 for OrthoLoRA), showing that the calibration knowledge transfers even to shifted distributions. This makes SBA practical for latency-critical deployments: train with SBA, distill, and deploy the deterministic student.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Related Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our work sits at the intersection of Bayesian PEFT, orthogonal adapters, calibration in NLP, and Riemannian methods.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al. (2024)</a></cite> apply variational inference to LoRA weights with Gaussian priors, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Onal et al. (2024)</a></cite> explore Laplace approximations for adapters. Both operate in flat Euclidean space, ignoring the geometric structure of the adapter parameter space. More recently, <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Daxberger et al. (2024)</a></cite> introduced Laplace-LoRA, applying a post-hoc Laplace approximation to LoRA parameters with strong calibration results, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lin and others (2025)</a></cite> demonstrated that effective uncertainty quantification can be achieved in very low-dimensional parameter subspaces. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sharma and others (2025)</a></cite> scale Bayesian LoRA via stochastic variational subspace inference, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Meo and others (2025)</a></cite> combine Bayesian gates with rank selection to jointly optimize adapter structure and uncertainty. All of these methods operate in flat Euclidean space. Our work demonstrates that manifold-aware priors yield fundamentally better uncertainty estimates, as evidenced by the consistent gap between SBA and Gauss+Proj across all evaluation settings and both model families. The Gauss+Proj baseline is the most informative comparison in our experiments, since it uses the same computational budget and the same manifold constraint at the MAP, differing only in the prior geometry. The consistent 18–33% ECE improvement of SBA over Gauss+Proj isolates the effect of the prior geometry from all other factors.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">OFT <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Qiu et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, Cayley-parameterized LoRA, and orthonormal LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang and others, 2024</a>)</cite> enforce orthogonality but remain deterministic. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hao and others (2024)</a></cite> apply Riemannian preconditioning to LoRA optimization, improving convergence but not providing uncertainty estimates, and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Muqeeth and others (2025)</a></cite> develop parametrization-independent optimizers for low-rank adapters on the fixed-rank manifold. SBA subsumes these as the MAP-only special case, extending them with principled uncertainty quantification. Post-hoc calibration methods such as temperature scaling <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Guo et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">Platt, 1999</a>)</cite> and isotonic regression are widely used but require held-out calibration data from the target domain. Ensemble methods <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">Lakshminarayanan et al., 2017</a>)</cite> provide uncertainty but at <math id="S6.p3.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times</annotation></semantics></math> the parameter cost; our results show that SBA matches or outperforms 5-model LoRA ensembles within a single model’s parameter budget. This is a significant practical advantage, since ensembles require <math id="S6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> independent training runs and <math id="S6.p3.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="N\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N\times</annotation></semantics></math> the storage and serving cost. The broader Laplace approximation framework for deep learning <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">Daxberger et al., 2021</a>)</cite> provides the foundation for our tangent space approach, though we extend it from flat Euclidean space to the Stiefel manifold. Other PEFT variants such as AdaLoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and QLoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">Dettmers et al., 2023</a>)</cite> focus on efficiency rather than uncertainty, and are complementary to our approach.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Optimization on Stiefel manifolds has been explored for various ML problems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Absil et al., 2008</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bécigneul and Ganea, 2019</a>)</cite>. Our contribution is not the Riemannian optimization machinery per se, but rather the formal connection between manifold priors and PEFT uncertainty (Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Geometric Variance Inflation &amp; KL Tightness). ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), showing that the choice of prior geometry has a direct and measurable impact on downstream reliability. To our knowledge, this is the first result establishing that the KL divergence of a manifold-aware posterior approximation strictly avoids the cross-coupled structural deterioration inherent to projected flat-space approximations for compact Riemannian submanifolds.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">More broadly, the question of how to certify the reliability of LLM outputs has received growing attention. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Akter et al. (2025)</a></cite> develop information-lift statistics for selective risk certification of LLM generations, achieving strong coverage-risk tradeoffs that complement the selective prediction framework we evaluate. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al. (2026)</a></cite> use Fisher-aligned subspace diagnostics for knowledge-aware LLM compression, demonstrating that subspace structure in the parameter space carries meaningful information about model behavior, a finding that resonates with our thesis that subspace geometry matters for uncertainty. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al. (2025b)</a></cite> propose differentiable entropy regularization for complexity-aware neural optimization, providing a complementary perspective on how entropy-based objectives can improve model reliability. More broadly, Bayesian posterior methods have been shown to be practical even in sequential decision-making settings with LLM-derived priors <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shihab et al., 2025a</a>)</cite>, suggesting that the scalable posterior inference techniques we develop here have applications beyond PEFT.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduced Stiefel-Bayes Adapters, a Bayesian PEFT framework that places Matrix Langevin priors on the Stiefel manifold of orthonormal adapter factors. Our tangent space Laplace approximation enables scalable posterior inference with minimal overhead, and we proved formally that this geometry-aware approximation completely avoids the structural variance inflation and geometric bias of the flat-space alternative.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The central finding is that geometric structure in the prior matters: SBA consistently outperforms flat-space Bayesian alternatives and deep ensembles on calibration, selective prediction, and OOD detection across two model families, with the largest gains appearing under domain shift. The benefits extend to generative tasks and survive predictive distillation, making SBA practical for deployment.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Looking forward, we see several promising directions. The tangent space Laplace framework is not specific to the Stiefel manifold; it could be applied to any Riemannian manifold used as a parameter space, such as the Grassmannian (for subspace-valued adapters) or the manifold of positive definite matrices (for covariance-structured adapters). The predictive distillation approach could be extended to preserve the full uncertainty decomposition, not just the averaged predictions, by training the student to match both the mean and variance of the teacher’s predictive distribution. Finally, combining SBA with active learning could yield PEFT methods that not only know when they are uncertain but actively seek out the most informative examples for fine-tuning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations</h2>

<div id="Sx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SBA introduces inference-time overhead from posterior sampling (<math id="Sx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> forward passes). While predictive distillation mitigates this (Section <a href="#S5.SS7" title="5.7 Predictive Distillation ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.7</span></a>), the distilled model does not retain the full uncertainty decomposition into aleatoric and epistemic components. Our experiments cover RoBERTa-large, LLaMA-2-7B, and LLaMA-2-13B; the consistent relative gains across these three scales suggest the geometric advantage persists, though behavior on 70B+ models remains to be validated. The tangent space Laplace approximation is local and may underestimate uncertainty far from the MAP; Riemannian MCMC methods could address this at higher computational cost. We validated the saddle-point approximation to the hypergeometric normalizing constant empirically and found relative error below 2% for the concentration values encountered during training (<math id="Sx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}\leq 5.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>≤</mo><mn>5.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}\leq 5.0</annotation></semantics></math>), but extreme concentrations may require more sophisticated approximations. Finally, our evaluation focuses on English-language tasks; the behavior of SBA under multilingual fine-tuning, where the adapter subspace structure may differ across languages, is an open question.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Ethics Statement</h2>

<div id="Sx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SBA is designed to improve the reliability of deployed NLP systems by providing calibrated uncertainty estimates. We believe this is a net positive for responsible AI deployment, since it enables systems to abstain on uncertain predictions rather than producing confident but incorrect outputs. However, we note that calibration is a necessary but not sufficient condition for safe deployment: a well-calibrated model can still produce harmful outputs with appropriate confidence. SBA should be used as one component of a broader safety framework, not as a standalone guarantee of reliability.</p>
</div>
</section>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Proof Details for Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Geometric Variance Inflation &amp; KL Tightness). ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a></h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We provide the step-by-step derivation of the geometric distortion induced by the polar projection <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\pi(W)=W(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>W</mi><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(W)=W(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>, expanding upon the algebraic sequence necessary to explicitly isolate the cross-coupling artifact.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}+\xi_{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=\hat{U}+\xi_{T}+\xi_{N}</annotation></semantics></math> be a perturbed sample drawn from the ambient Gaussian, where <math id="A1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{T}\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{T}\in T_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{N}\in N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{N}\in N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math>. Because <math id="A1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>St</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> defines orthonormal columns, its normal space <math id="A1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>St</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\hat{U}}\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math> comprises elements of the form <math id="A1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{N}=\hat{U}S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{N}=\hat{U}S</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k}</annotation></semantics></math> is any symmetric matrix.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the projection <math id="A1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi(W)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi(W)</annotation></semantics></math> directly. First, we compute the Gram matrix <math id="A1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{\top}W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>W</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{\top}W</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="A1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="A1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> is confined to the tangent space at <math id="A1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}</annotation></semantics></math>, it strictly satisfies the differential metric equation <math id="A1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. The Gram matrix simplifies to:</p>

<div id="A1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Next, we extract the inverse square root <math id="A1.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W^{\top}W)^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> utilizing the matrix Taylor expansion <math id="A1.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="(I+X)^{-1/2}=I-\frac{1}{2}X+\frac{3}{8}X^{2}+O(\|X\|^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>I</mi><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mi>X</mi><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>O</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>X</mi><msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(I+X)^{-1/2}=I-\frac{1}{2}X+\frac{3}{8}X^{2}+O(\|X\|^{3})</annotation></semantics></math>. Substituting the perturbation matrix <math id="A1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X=2S+\xi_{T}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}+S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X=2S+\xi_{T}^{\top}\xi_{T}+\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}+S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> yields:</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\quad+S^{2}+O(\|\xi\|^{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>3</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\quad+S^{2}+O(\|\xi\|^{3})</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
<div id="A1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We apply this operator back to <math id="A1.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W=\hat{U}(I_{k}+S)+\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W=\hat{U}(I_{k}+S)+\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> to complete the projection <math id="A1.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<div id="A1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Conversely, any standard second-order constraint-preserving retraction <math id="A1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> on the Stiefel manifold (such as the exponential map, Cayley retraction, or QR/polar applied purely to tangent vectors) enforces exact intrinsic tangent integration:</p>

<div id="A1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The strict difference between the projected ambient posterior and the retracted intrinsic posterior is the structural distortion quantity <math id="A1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S-\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S-\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p7.2" class="ltx_p">Because <math id="A1.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}=-\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}=-\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}</annotation></semantics></math>, we can rewrite <math id="A1.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S=\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\xi_{T}^{\top}\hat{U}S=\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus,</p>
<table id="A1.Ex22" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex22.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S+\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="false"><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta(\xi_{T},\xi_{N})=-\xi_{T}S+\tfrac{1}{2}\hat{U}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p7.3" class="ltx_p">To verify <math id="A1.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is strictly a tangent vector, we check the metric condition <math id="A1.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta+\Delta^{\top}\hat{U}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta+\Delta^{\top}\hat{U}=0</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx5" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex23"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex23.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=-\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S+\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S+\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S-S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.Ex24"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex24.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=-\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=-\tfrac{1}{2}(\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}S+S\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p7.4" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A1.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math> is skew-symmetric, let <math id="A1.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ξ</mi><mi>T</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=\hat{U}^{\top}\xi_{T}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then <math id="A1.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta=-\frac{1}{2}(KS+SK)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta=-\frac{1}{2}(KS+SK)</annotation></semantics></math>. Because <math id="A1.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>S</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S</annotation></semantics></math> is symmetric and <math id="A1.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> is skew-symmetric:</p>
<table id="A1.Ex25" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(KS+SK)^{\top}=S^{\top}K^{\top}+K^{\top}S^{\top}=S(-K)+(-K)S=-(KS+SK)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>K</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(KS+SK)^{\top}=S^{\top}K^{\top}+K^{\top}S^{\top}=S(-K)+(-K)S=-(KS+SK)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.p7.5" class="ltx_p">Thus <math id="A1.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is precisely skew-symmetric, confirming <math id="A1.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta+\Delta^{\top}\hat{U}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>U</mi><mo>^</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{U}^{\top}\Delta+\Delta^{\top}\hat{U}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, meaning <math id="A1.p7.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> resides entirely in the tangent space.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p8.1" class="ltx_p">This mathematically proves that the normal-space variance from ambient approximations artificially and unavoidably couples into the tangent space, inflating the effective posterior variance and necessitating the purely intrinsic tangent-space approach.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Reliability Diagram Details</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reliability diagrams (Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5.2 In-Distribution Results ‣ 5 Experiments ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) use 15 equal-width bins on the confidence axis <math id="A2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. We plot the mean observed accuracy within each bin against the mean predicted confidence. Error bars show <math id="A2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm 1</annotation></semantics></math> standard deviation across 5 seeds. The gap between the bar height and the diagonal represents calibration error for that bin; the area-weighted sum of these gaps is the ECE.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A3" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix C </span>Normalizer Approximation Validation</h2>

<div id="A3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We validated the saddle-point approximation to the hypergeometric normalizing constant <math id="A3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{0}F_{1}(\tfrac{d}{2};\tfrac{1}{4}F^{\top}F)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>F</mi><mprescripts></mprescripts><mn>1</mn><mrow></mrow><mn>0</mn><mrow></mrow></mmultiscripts><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>,</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{0}F_{1}(\tfrac{d}{2};\tfrac{1}{4}F^{\top}F)</annotation></semantics></math> by comparing against Monte Carlo estimates (<math id="A3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> samples from the Haar measure on <math id="A3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{St}(k,d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>St</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{St}(k,d)</annotation></semantics></math>) for <math id="A3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\in\{64,128,256,512\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>64,128,256,512</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\in\{64,128,256,512\}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{4,8,16\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{4,8,16\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}\in\{0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0,5.0\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0.1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0.5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2.0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5.0</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}\in\{0.1,0.5,1.0,2.0,5.0\}</annotation></semantics></math>. The relative error of the saddle-point approximation is below 0.5% for <math id="A3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\geq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\geq 128</annotation></semantics></math> and below 2% for <math id="A3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d=64" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d=64</annotation></semantics></math>, across all tested <math id="A3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> values. The gradient error (relevant for MAP training) is even smaller, below 0.1% for <math id="A3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\geq 128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\geq 128</annotation></semantics></math>, confirming that the approximation does not introduce meaningful bias into the optimization.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Extended In-Distribution Results</h2>

<div id="A4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report additional GLUE/SuperGLUE results on RTE and BoolQ for both model families. On RTE (LLaMA-2-7B), SBA achieves accuracy <math id="A4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.3_{\pm 0.8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>82.3</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.3_{\pm 0.8}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".038_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.038</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.038_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="A4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.1_{\pm 0.9}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>82.1</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.1_{\pm 0.9}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".071_{\pm.006}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.071</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.006</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.071_{\pm.006}</annotation></semantics></math> and Deep-Ens-LoRA at <math id="A4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="82.5_{\pm 0.5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>82.5</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">82.5_{\pm 0.5}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".042_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.042</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.042_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math>. On BoolQ (LLaMA-2-7B), SBA achieves accuracy <math id="A4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.7_{\pm 0.3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>86.7</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.3</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.7_{\pm 0.3}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".029_{\pm.002}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.029</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.002</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.029_{\pm.002}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="A4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.5_{\pm 0.4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>86.5</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.5_{\pm 0.4}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".054_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.054</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.054_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and Deep-Ens-LoRA at <math id="A4.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="86.8_{\pm 0.2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>86.8</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.2</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">86.8_{\pm 0.2}</annotation></semantics></math> with ECE <math id="A4.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".033_{\pm.002}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.033</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.002</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.033_{\pm.002}</annotation></semantics></math>. The pattern is consistent across all tasks: SBA matches or slightly trails the best deterministic method on accuracy while achieving the best calibration, outperforming even the 5-model ensemble.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On RoBERTa-large, the results follow the same trend. RTE: SBA accuracy <math id="A4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="80.1_{\pm 1.0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>80.1</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80.1_{\pm 1.0}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECE <math id="A4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".035_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.035</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.035_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> vs. LoRA accuracy <math id="A4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="79.8_{\pm 1.1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>79.8</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1.1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">79.8_{\pm 1.1}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECE <math id="A4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".068_{\pm.006}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.068</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.006</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.068_{\pm.006}</annotation></semantics></math>. BoolQ: SBA accuracy <math id="A4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.9_{\pm 0.4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>84.9</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.4</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.9_{\pm 0.4}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECE <math id="A4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".027_{\pm.003}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.027</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.003</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.027_{\pm.003}</annotation></semantics></math> vs. LoRA accuracy <math id="A4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="84.7_{\pm 0.5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>84.7</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>0.5</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">84.7_{\pm 0.5}</annotation></semantics></math>, ECE <math id="A4.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".051_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.051</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.051_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Distillation Details</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The predictive distillation procedure trains a deterministic OrthoLoRA student to match the SBA teacher’s averaged predictive distribution. Specifically, for each training example <math id="A5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>, we compute the SBA predictive distribution <math id="A5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{p}(y\mid x)=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^{S}p(y\mid x,U^{(s)},\Sigma^{(s)},V^{(s)})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>S</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>s</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>S</mi></msubsup><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>U</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>V</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{p}(y\mid x)=\frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^{S}p(y\mid x,U^{(s)},\Sigma^{(s)},V^{(s)})</annotation></semantics></math> using <math id="A5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> posterior samples, then minimize <math id="A5.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathrm{KL}(\bar{p}\|p_{\text{student}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>KL</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mtext>student</mtext></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{KL}(\bar{p}\|p_{\text{student}})</annotation></semantics></math> with temperature <math id="A5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=2.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=2.0</annotation></semantics></math>. The student is initialized from the SBA MAP estimate and trained for 1 additional epoch with learning rate <math id="A5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>. This procedure takes approximately 20% of the original training time since it requires only forward passes through the teacher (no gradient computation for the teacher) and a single backward pass through the student.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>Wall-Clock Timing Breakdown</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report wall-clock times for the key components of SBA training and inference on LLaMA-2-7B with MNLI, measured on a single A100 GPU.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Training (per epoch): LoRA takes 42 minutes, OrthoLoRA takes 44 minutes (5% overhead from Stiefel projection), and SBA takes 45 minutes (7% overhead from Riemannian gradient projection). The Hessian computation at the end of training takes 5 minutes over 1024 data points.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Inference (per 1000 examples): LoRA takes 18 seconds, SBA with <math id="A6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=5</annotation></semantics></math> takes 90 seconds, SBA with <math id="A6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=10</annotation></semantics></math> takes 180 seconds, and the distilled SBA student takes 18 seconds (identical to LoRA). Deep-Ens-LoRA with 5 models takes 90 seconds, matching SBA at <math id="A6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S=5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S=5</annotation></semantics></math> but requiring <math id="A6.p3.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math> the GPU memory for the ensemble weights.</p>
</div>
<div id="A6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The key takeaway is that SBA’s training overhead is negligible (7%), and the inference overhead is comparable to a deep ensemble at the same number of forward passes, but with <math id="A6.p4.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\times</annotation></semantics></math> less memory.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Per-Seed Variance Analysis</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report the coefficient of variation (std / mean) of ECE across 5 seeds for each method on MNLI (LLaMA-2-7B). LoRA has CV 6.6%, Laplace-LoRA has CV 7.7%, Gauss+Proj has CV 8.3%, Deep-Ens-LoRA has CV 6.7%, and SBA has CV 7.4%. The variance of SBA’s calibration is comparable to other methods, indicating that the geometric prior does not introduce additional instability. The slightly higher variance of Gauss+Proj is consistent with the projection problem discussed in Section <a href="#S4" title="4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>: the polar projection introduces stochastic variance distortion that varies across seeds.</p>
</div>
<div id="A7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On RoBERTa-large, the pattern is similar: SBA has ECE CV of 8.0%, LoRA has 7.2%, and Gauss+Proj has 8.8%. The slightly higher variance on the smaller model is expected, since the adapter subspaces are lower-dimensional and the posterior is less concentrated.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Uncertainty Decomposition Analysis</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">SBA’s predictive distribution naturally decomposes into aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. The total predictive entropy <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H[p(y\mid x,\mathcal{D})]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H[p(y\mid x,\mathcal{D})]</annotation></semantics></math> equals the sum of the expected entropy <math id="A8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[H[p(y\mid x,\theta)]]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>H</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{E}_{\theta}[H[p(y\mid x,\theta)]]</annotation></semantics></math> (aleatoric, reflecting inherent label ambiguity) and the mutual information <math id="A8.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="I(y;\theta\mid x,\mathcal{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>;</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I(y;\theta\mid x,\mathcal{D})</annotation></semantics></math> (epistemic, reflecting model ignorance).</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On MNLI in-distribution, the epistemic component accounts for 28% of total uncertainty on average. On the MNLI <math id="A8.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI shift, this rises to 41%, confirming that the manifold posterior correctly attributes increased uncertainty to model ignorance rather than data noise. For comparison, Gauss+Proj shows epistemic fractions of 22% (in-distribution) and 31% (shifted), indicating that the flat-space posterior underestimates epistemic uncertainty under shift. This underestimation is precisely what Theorem <a href="#Thmtheorem1" title="Theorem 1 (Geometric Variance Inflation &amp; KL Tightness). ‣ 4 Why Geometry Matters: Formal Analysis ‣ Calibrated Adaptation: Bayesian Stiefel Manifold Priorsfor Reliable Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> predicts: the normal-space variance in Gauss+Proj inflates the apparent posterior width without contributing genuine epistemic signal.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">On the OOD detection task (SST-2 vs. 20 Newsgroups), the epistemic component accounts for 72% of total uncertainty on OOD examples but only 28% on in-distribution examples. This clean separation is what enables SBA’s strong OOD detection: the mutual information alone achieves AUROC .941, slightly higher than the .934 achieved by total predictive entropy, suggesting that the epistemic component is the more informative signal for OOD detection.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A9" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix I </span>RoBERTa-large Domain Shift Results</h2>

<div id="A9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report domain shift results on RoBERTa-large for the MNLI <math id="A9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\to" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\to</annotation></semantics></math> SNLI shift. SBA achieves ECE <math id="A9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".053_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.053</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.053_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and selective AUROC <math id="A9.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".808_{\pm.008}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.808</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.008</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.808_{\pm.008}</annotation></semantics></math>, compared to LoRA at <math id="A9.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".102_{\pm.007}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.102</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.007</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.102_{\pm.007}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A9.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".698_{\pm.013}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.698</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.013</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.698_{\pm.013}</annotation></semantics></math>, Laplace-LoRA at <math id="A9.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".076_{\pm.005}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.076</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.005</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.076_{\pm.005}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A9.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".755_{\pm.011}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.755</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.011</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.755_{\pm.011}</annotation></semantics></math>, and Deep-Ens-LoRA at <math id="A9.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".062_{\pm.004}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.062</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.004</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.062_{\pm.004}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A9.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".789_{\pm.008}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mn>.789</mn><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>.008</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.789_{\pm.008}</annotation></semantics></math>. The pattern matches the LLaMA-2-7B results: SBA provides the best calibration and selective prediction, outperforming even the 5-model ensemble. The relative improvement of SBA over Gauss+Proj is 24% on ECE (<math id="A9.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".053" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.053</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.053</annotation></semantics></math> vs. <math id="A9.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext=".070" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>.070</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">.070</annotation></semantics></math>), consistent with the 28% improvement observed on LLaMA-2-7B.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A10" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix J </span>Hyperparameter Details</h2>

<figure id="A10.T10" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>Hyperparameters for SBA and baselines.</figcaption>
<table id="A10.T10.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="A10.T10.2.1" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A10.T10.2.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt">Parameter</td>
<td id="A10.T10.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_tt">Value</td></tr>
<tr id="A10.T10.2.2" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A10.T10.2.2.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">Adapter rank <math id="A10.T10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td id="A10.T10.2.2.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_border_t">16</td></tr>
<tr id="A10.T10.2.3" class="ltx_tr">
<td id="A10.T10.2.3.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left">Prior concentration <math id="A10.T10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
